*UW–Madison · PSYC 752 Machine Learning*

Adapted from John Curtin’s Unit 4 classification lab and starter Quarto template. I engineered passenger features and compared four preprocessing recipes at three neighborhood sizes. The age-band model with 35 neighbors achieved the highest KNN validation accuracy at **82.1%**.

## Data and evaluation

The outcome is passenger survival. I fit each KNN model on the course training split and compared classification accuracy on the validation split. The recipes standardize numeric predictors and one-hot encode categorical predictors for the distance calculation.

To render this report, install the R packages tidymodels, kknn, and stringr. Put the two cleaned course CSVs listed below in a local `data/` directory next to this file, then run `quarto render fit_knn.qmd` from the repository root.

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(tidymodels)
library(stringr)

data_dir <- "data"

read_split <- function(filename) {
  read_csv(file.path(data_dir, filename), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    mutate(
      across(where(is.character), as.factor),
      survived = as.factor(survived)
    )
}

data_trn <- read_split("titanic_train_cln.csv")
data_val <- read_split("titanic_val_cln.csv")
```

## Feature engineering

### Cabin deck and family size

I took the first character of the cabin code to represent deck, pooled rare deck levels, and summed the relative counts plus the passenger to represent family size. I used an LLM to help with preprocessing in this recipe.

```{r}
#| label: recipe-1

rec_m1 <- recipe(survived ~ ., data = data_trn) |>
  update_role(passenger_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_select(
    survived, passenger_id,
    age, fare, n_sib_spouse, n_parent_child,
    embarked, cabin) |>
  step_mutate(family_size = n_sib_spouse + n_parent_child + 1) |>
  step_mutate(
    cabin_deck = case_when(
      is.na(cabin) | cabin == "" ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ str_sub(cabin, 1, 1))) |>
  step_other(cabin_deck, threshold = 0.05, other = "Other") |>
  step_rm(cabin) |>
  # llm helped me 
  step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_unknown(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE)
```

### Age bands

I grouped age into child, young adult, adult, and older adult bands to compare passengers using broad age categories.

```{r}
#| label: recipe-2

rec_m2 <- recipe(survived ~ ., data = data_trn) |>
  update_role(passenger_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_select(
    survived, passenger_id,
    age, fare, n_sib_spouse, n_parent_child,
    sex, embarked) |>
  step_mutate(
    age_group = case_when(
      age < 12  ~ "child",
      age < 30  ~ "young_adult",
      age < 55  ~ "adult",
      age >= 55 ~ "older_adult",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_)) |>
  step_rm(age) |>
  step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_unknown(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE)
```

### Fare bands and fare per family member

I divided fare by recorded family size and grouped fares into quartile-based bands. The original recipe computes the fare cut points separately on the training and validation splits when generating features.

```{r}
#| label: recipe-3

rec_m3 <- recipe(survived ~ ., data = data_trn) |>
  update_role(passenger_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_select(
    survived, passenger_id,
    age, fare, n_sib_spouse, n_parent_child,
    pclass, sex) |>
  step_mutate(
    family_size = n_sib_spouse + n_parent_child + 1,
    fare_per_person = fare / family_size) |>
  step_mutate(
    fare_group = cut(
      fare,
      breaks = quantile(fare, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.25), na.rm = TRUE),
      include.lowest = TRUE,
      labels = c("low", "mid_low", "mid_high", "high"))) |>
  step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_unknown(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE)
```

### Ticket prefixes and family size

I extracted the letter prefixes from tickets, grouped tickets without a letter prefix, and pooled rare groups. This recipe also includes family size and continuous age.

```{r}
#| label: recipe-4

rec_m4 <- recipe(survived ~ ., data = data_trn) |>
  update_role(passenger_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_select(
    survived, passenger_id,
    age, fare, n_sib_spouse, n_parent_child,
    sex, embarked, ticket
  ) |>
  step_mutate(family_size = n_sib_spouse + n_parent_child + 1) |>
  step_mutate(
    ticket_group = case_when(
      is.na(ticket) | ticket == "" ~ "Unknown",
      str_detect(ticket, "^[A-Za-z]") ~ str_extract(ticket, "^[A-Za-z]+"),
      TRUE ~ "NUM")) |>
  step_other(ticket_group, threshold = 0.05, other = "Other") |>
  step_rm(ticket) |>
  step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_unknown(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE)
```

## Validation results

These are the validation accuracies from the original course run. The recipes change several features at once, so the scores compare complete configurations.

| Configuration | k = 5 | k = 15 | k = 35 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cabin deck and family size | 69.1% | 71.1% | 72.0% |
| Age bands | 79.3% | 81.3% | **82.1%** |
| Fare bands and fare per family member | 77.6% | 81.3% | 80.5% |
| Ticket prefixes and family size | 78.5% | 81.3% | 80.9% |

The recipes mark `passenger_id` as an ID, but the original `survived ~ .` formula can still include it as a predictor when fitting directly on the baked data. The code below preserves that formula so the comparison reflects the original run.

```{r}
#| label: validation

evaluate_knn <- function(feature_recipe) {
  prepared_recipe <- prep(feature_recipe, training = data_trn)
  train_features <- bake(prepared_recipe, new_data = NULL)
  validation_features <- bake(prepared_recipe, new_data = data_val)
  neighbor_counts <- c(5L, 15L, 35L)

  scores <- vapply(neighbor_counts, function(k) {
    model <- nearest_neighbor(neighbors = k) |>
      set_engine("kknn") |>
      set_mode("classification") |>
      fit(survived ~ ., data = train_features)

    predictions <- predict(model, validation_features)$.pred_class
    accuracy_vec(validation_features$survived, predictions)
  }, numeric(1))

  tibble(neighbors = neighbor_counts, validation_accuracy = scores)
}

validation_results <- bind_rows(
  "Cabin deck and family size" = evaluate_knn(rec_m1),
  "Age bands" = evaluate_knn(rec_m2),
  "Fare bands and fare per family member" = evaluate_knn(rec_m3),
  "Ticket prefixes and family size" = evaluate_knn(rec_m4),
  .id = "configuration"
)

knitr::kable(validation_results, digits = 3)
```
